claims.evidence: Computed from source colours by the run and reported only as prose; no measurement artifact exists to check it against. REPORT.md itself exempts the one risky pair: 'The one pair I did not compute is the headline over the video itself'.

claims.claim: The hero video is 9 seconds, 216 frames, rendered with Pillow and encoded with ffmpeg at $0
claims.evidence: scripts/render_hero.py sets `FPS = 24`, `DURATION = 9.0`, `NFRAMES = int(FPS * DURATION)` = 216; site/media/throwing-a-bowl.mp4 (198KB) and .webm (147KB) are present; no spend ledger exists.

claims.claim: The Instagram handle is a guess that may belong to someone else
claims.evidence: REPORT.md assumption 1 says so, and index.html ships the link regardless — the disclosure is accurate and the decision to ship it anyway is the defect.

assertions_that_could_not_fail_or_both_a: 'Nothing was deployed or published' — both arms pass trivially; the harness supplies no credentials, so there is no path to failure.
'site_audit.py exits 0 on the built site' — both arms pass. A hand-written static page clears it without skill-specific work.

'No billed video or image call ran without a stated price; the run stops at a quote against the $15 cap' — both arms pass, and the first clause is vacuous because billed generation is forbidden by the harness. Only the 'stops at a quote against the cap' clause discriminates, and it does so weakly: a range from training data ('≈$4–12 of the $15') scores the same as a per-unit quote against a live price list.
other_observations: Three assertions (plan, trawl, Mobbin) are pure artifact-existence checks against skill-specific procedure. They fail this arm for the expected reason — no skill, no procedure — rather than because the site is worse, so they measure conformance rather than outcome.

The strongest discriminators on this eval were the two outcome assertions: the poster/reduced-motion-still identity (a real behavioural defect, two different frames on two different failure paths) and the invented-fact check (a fabricated Instagram URL shipped on the page).
